12.2.1 A Late Answer Has Nobody to Go To

gates.says: all 4 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-silent-firewall-server: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-silent-firewall-server: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-silent-firewall-server: 12.4 'On the server' bullet: the terminal reconnects on a new session, the old session stays open forever, and weeks later the QServer reaches its session limit and refuses new connections, which is option c.
recorded.prompt:q-terminal-gives-up-first: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-terminal-gives-up-first: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-terminal-gives-up-first: 12.4: 'If the terminal gives up at 30 seconds and you wait 45, a host approval at 40 seconds becomes a payment the terminal has already shown as failed', which is option b.
recorded.prompt:q-echo-slower-than-timeout: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-echo-slower-than-timeout: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-echo-slower-than-timeout: 12.4 requires 'echo interval < read timeout', and the 12.9 table says `timeout` fires when no byte is read for that long and the client reconnects, so with a 10-minute echo and a 6-minute timeout the link is closed and reopened repeatedly (option d).
recorded.prompt:q-late-approval: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-late-approval: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-late-approval: 12.2.1: QMUX 'found nobody waiting', offered the message to its request-listeners, and since none took it 'put it on the <unhandled> queue'; 12.1 configures <unhandled>, so the answer is option a.

gates.says: all 12 of this quiz's discriminating readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-silent-firewall-server:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-silent-firewall-server:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-silent-firewall-server:a: 12.4 says the terminal reconnects on a new session and the old one 'stays open forever', so reconnecting does not close it.
recorded.prompt:q-silent-firewall-server:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-silent-firewall-server:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-silent-firewall-server:b: 12.4 says the QServer 'reaches its session limit and refuses new connections', so the slots are not reused.
recorded.prompt:q-silent-firewall-server:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-silent-firewall-server:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-silent-firewall-server:d: 12.4 says the firewall drops sessions silently ('neither side receives anything') and the server's old session stays open.
recorded.prompt:q-terminal-gives-up-first:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-terminal-gives-up-first:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-terminal-gives-up-first:a: The same 12.4 sentence says the approval at 40 becomes a payment, so the host does not treat the purchase as failed; that QMUX does not drop it at 30 follows from the 45-second request timeout.
recorded.prompt:q-terminal-gives-up-first:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-terminal-gives-up-first:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-terminal-gives-up-first:c: By short inference: 12.4 says the approval becomes a payment the terminal showed as failed, so the records do not agree, and 12.5-12.7 present reversals as application code (ReversalBuilder, ReversalSaf).
recorded.prompt:q-terminal-gives-up-first:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-terminal-gives-up-first:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-terminal-gives-up-first:d: 12.4 says the terminal 'has already shown [it] as failed' at 30 seconds, so it is not waiting at 40.
recorded.prompt:q-echo-slower-than-timeout:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-echo-slower-than-timeout:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-echo-slower-than-timeout:a: 12.9 table: the timeout fires after 6 minutes with no byte read, before the 10-minute echo arrives, and 12.4 says echoes must come more often than the read timeout.
recorded.prompt:q-echo-slower-than-timeout:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-echo-slower-than-timeout:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-echo-slower-than-timeout:b: 12.9 table defines the channel `timeout` as 'no byte is read for that long', with no condition about a waiting request, and 12.4 separates it from the request timeout.
recorded.prompt:q-echo-slower-than-timeout:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-echo-slower-than-timeout:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-echo-slower-than-timeout:c: By short inference from the 12.9 definition ('no byte is read for that long'): after a reconnect the quiet periods continue and the timeout fires again.
recorded.prompt:q-late-approval:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-late-approval:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-late-approval:b: 12.2.1 says an unmatched message goes to the request-listeners and then the unhandled queue (or is silently dropped); nothing is sent back to the host.
recorded.prompt:q-late-approval:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-late-approval:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-late-approval:c: 12.2 says a response is matched to a request by key (MTI, field 41, STAN), so it cannot go to an unrelated next request.
recorded.prompt:q-late-approval:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-late-approval:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-late-approval:d: 12.2.1 says request returned null and QMUX 'found nobody waiting', so there is no grace period.
